attributes.cost_breakdown:
1. ONB - Onboarding (Automated dev env setup, Documentation, Smart Contracts Catalogue) = 0,25 FTE = $23 750 = ₳36 538,46 

2. SC - Smart Contracts (Simple syntax, standard library, blueprint implementation) = 0,75 FTE = $71 250 = ₳109 615,38

3. ADV - Advanced UPLC (Advanced optimisations, Expression builder, pattern matching, macros) = 0,75 FTE =  $71 250 = ₳109 615,38

4. MPL - Off-chain libraries (Exportable multi-platform library - JVM/JS/TS/Native) = 0,25 FTE = $23 750 = ₳36 538,46

5. TEST - Testing capabilities (Scalus Test library, Property-based testing enablers) = 0,5 FTE = $47 500 = ₳73 076,92

6. INT - Integration / Deployment (Local network/node for testing, deployment to mainnet) = 0,5 FTE = $47 500 = ₳73 076,92

7. MAN - Maintenance (Maintenance, bug-fixing and support) = 1 FTE = $95 000 = ₳146 153,85

8. PM - Product management (Management of the product life cycle) = 0,5 FTE = $47 500 = ₳73 076,92


We are projecting 6 months of development and maintenance (starting from June 2025 to the end of the year).

All the scopes are estimated in FTE (Full Time Employee). For the sake of evaluating the budget, we took the assumption that one Senior Scala Engineer / Senior Product Manager with expertise in DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) is valued at $190k (recruitment, on-boarding and extra costs related to working – i.e paid vacations, sick leave – are considered included in the $190k figure).

attributes.proposal_description:
Developing DApps on Cardano shouldn't require juggling multiple languages, libraries and frameworks.

Scalus changes this by bringing the power of Scala 3 to the Cardano ecosystem, letting you write smart contracts, build transactions, and application layers — all with the same language and familiar tools.

It supports the complete development flow - setup, development, testing, debugging and deployment, backed by an industry-grade toolset and professional development experience.

Key benefits that make Scalus + Scala 3 stand out:
- Productivity boost at scale with Scala 3
- Reduced time-to-market - from prototyping to production in less time
- Deep pool of Scala/Java/Kotlin talent available on the market

Scalus is a Cardano DApps development platform made for professionals and businesses who want to get things done.

More details in the attached presentation.

- Q3 2025 - Serialisation / deserialisation
- Q4 2025 - Transaction builder - Enrichment
- Q3 2025 - Evaluation & cost function
- Q4 2025 - Domain objects & ledger rules

attributes.problem_statement:
Building DApps on Cardano remains harder than it should be. New developers need to invest a substantial amount of time to become productive. It makes Cardano less attractive to build on, and limits the ability to innovate and produce value to end users.

New developers face multiple obstacles:
1. Steep technical learning curve
2. Fragmented technology stack (on-chain/off-chain, front-end/back-end)
3. Limited development tooling and standard libraries
4. Scattered educational resources

In anticipation of the wider adoption of Cardano technology by traditional organisations (e.g., in finance and fintech, where Java and Scala are dominant), it should be simpler for their web2 developers to start building on Cardano. Companies need a smooth path for their existing teams — without the need to learn new programming languages or hire specialists just to get started.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
(1) Benefits for professionals

Scalus meets developers where they are. It bridges Web2 engineers from traditional firms with progressive onboarding and built-in safety, while giving seasoned Cardano builders advanced control and optimisations.

Web 2 developers:
- Familiar dev experience & tooling using Scala
- Elegant syntax with gentle learning curve of blockchain specifics
- Built-in safety controls to reduce common mistakes and risks

Cardano builders / R&D Labs:
- Low-level optimisations (memory, cost, advanced patterns)
- Expressiveness beyond limited DSL
- Advanced features (macros, meta-programming)
- Rich Scala ecosystem for complex protocols and mission-critical solutions

(2) Benefits for businesses

Scalus, paired with Scala 3, helps businesses build on Cardano without the usual headaches. It’s a practical way to deliver value quickly and reliably.

Benefits:
- Productivity boost at scale with Scala 3
- Reduced time-to-market - from prototyping to production in less time
- Deep pool of Scala/Java/Kotlin talent available on the market
- Code quality and safety are first-class citizens
- Reduced training investments to transition Scala/Java/Kotlin teams to blockchain
attributes.supplementary_endorsement:
Scalus is currently in the early adoption phase, emphasising close collaboration with the selected partners (individuals & businesses). It allows our team to:
- fine-tune the syntax & standard-library
- learn the preferences of the target groups
- iteratively grow the solution to answer those needs

Solutions in development with Scalus:
- Hydrozoa L2 - an evolution of the Hydra Head protocol (full stack development, node, networking, L2 ledger rules, transaction building)
- Innovative L2 protocol - block producing node MVP and related components
- Lucid Evolution - an alternative Scalus native JS implementation of serialisation/deserialization functions
- Script evaluation and cost calculation libraries used by the Cardano Foundation
- Cardano Client Lib (Java TxBuilder library) integration with the Scalus Smart Contracts evaluator

Two businesses participated in the early adoption program:
- Guild1 - expressed the interest in using the platform for future projects
- Proof Space Trusted Identity - implemented one of their components using Scalus

attributes.problem_statement:
Building DApps on Cardano remains harder than it should be. New developers need to invest a substantial amount of time to become productive. It makes Cardano less attractive to build on, and limits the ability to innovate and produce value to end users.

New developers face multiple obstacles:
1. Steep technical learning curve
2. Fragmented technology stack (on-chain/off-chain, front-end/back-end)
3. Limited development tooling and standard libraries
4. Scattered educational resources

In anticipation of the wider adoption of Cardano technology by traditional organisations (e.g., in finance and fintech, where Java and Scala are dominant), it should be simpler for their web2 developers to start building on Cardano. Companies need a smooth path for their existing teams — without the need to learn new programming languages or hire specialists just to get started.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
(1) Benefits for professionals

Scalus meets developers where they are. It bridges Web2 engineers from traditional firms with progressive onboarding and built-in safety, while giving seasoned Cardano builders advanced control and optimisations.

Web 2 developers:
- Familiar dev experience & tooling using Scala
- Elegant syntax with gentle learning curve of blockchain specifics
- Built-in safety controls to reduce common mistakes and risks

Cardano builders / R&D Labs:
- Low-level optimisations (memory, cost, advanced patterns)
- Expressiveness beyond limited DSL
- Advanced features (macros, meta-programming)
- Rich Scala ecosystem for complex protocols and mission-critical solutions

(2) Benefits for businesses

Scalus, paired with Scala 3, helps businesses build on Cardano without the usual headaches. It’s a practical way to deliver value quickly and reliably.

Benefits:

---- Dependencies to previous Catalyst proposals -----

We were awarded 2 Catalyst proposals in Fund 11 (on-boarding - March of 2024, totalling 328k ADA, approx. 150k USD). 
This funding (in addition to our own investment) supported us to deliver the core functionalities and bootstrap the key features of the Scalus development platform.

Notable achievements:
- Writing Cardano smart contracts in Scala 3
- Scala-to-UPLC compiler (with full support for Plutus v1, v2, v3)
- Script evaluation and cost calculation library with multi-platform support (JVM/JavaScript/Native) from the same codebase
- Integration with testing libraries
- Starter kit and first version of the documentation

We also received support for another proposal in Fund 13 (on-boarding in January of 2025, 100k ADA, approx. 60k USD). 
Prototyping of the off-chain transaction builder is currently underway.

These functionalities form the foundation of Scalus, which aims to be the DApps development platform of choice for professionals and businesses who want to get things done efficiently and effectively.

Our budget proposal is a follow-up, and a roadmap towards the platform vision, that consists of covering:
- Full-stack DApp development - on-chain, off-chain, and application layers.
- Complete development flow - setup, development, testing, debugging and deployment – all in one platform

---- Early adoption & interest ----

Our product development methodology enables us to iterate rapidly (1-2 week iterations) and learn and improve from the feedback provided by our early adopters.

Thank you for your thoughtful review of our proposal and the insightful questions raised. We're grateful for the effort you've put in understanding the essence and context of our work.

Before addressing the specific questions, I want to highlight that choosing Scala 3 for Scalus is a deliberate decision aimed at improving the developer experience to: boost team productivity, reduce DApp time-to-market, and onboard JVM developers into the Cardano ecosystem. Scalus is built on our experience in architecting enterprise applications (finance/fintech) and accelerating product development at scale (real estate/critical communications).

— So, why did we choose Scala 3? —

Scala 3 is part of the broader JVM ecosystem alongside Java and Kotlin, with full interoperability across these languages. JVM languages represent over 30% of the market and are especially strong in finance and fintech.

The Cardano ecosystem already uses JVM languages, such as:
- Moneta (USDM), written in Kotlin — we are in discussions with them to support their development with Scalus libraries;
- Reeve by the Cardano Foundation, built in Java (uses Cardano Client Lib, integrated with Scalus)

Scala 3 is well suited for Cardano DApp development, offering:
- A powerful type system for safety,
- Advanced productivity features (macros, pattern matching, implicits, etc),
- Multi-platform support (JVM, JavaScript, Native), existing adoption: Cardano Client Lib (Java) already uses Scalus; Lucid Evolution and MeshJS are planning integrations,
- Access to a mature JVM ecosystem and enterprise-grade development tools (for example: full DApp development in one project, working advanced debugger, Copilot trained on 2 billion lines of Scala Open Source code, etc)

In short, Scala 3 brings a modern, productive, and enterprise-grade development experience that can accelerate DApp and protocol development on Cardano.

— Why is additional funding critical at this stage, considering previous Catalyst support for foundational work? —

The foundational work funded through Catalyst — smart contract development, multi-platform evaluation, and transaction building — was essential to validate our hypothesis and prouve product viability.

Our modest early adoption program showed strong traction:
- Hydrozoa L2 — powered by Scalus,
- Innovative L2 — block-producing node MVP,
- Cardano Client Lib / Lucid Evolution / MeshJS — integrations of our evaluation libraries.

This encouraged us to pursue Scalus vision. Our current proposal is a natural follow-up and roadmap towards it.

We work in fast iterations (2-week cycles), learning directly from early adopters. This revealed specific needs:
- better onboarding and tutorials,
- improved syntax and standard libraries,
- customisable ledger rule sets for L2s protocols,
- faster DApp end-to-end testing, and more.

On top of this, we are offering the tailored support, code review and guidance for the tooling/design choices. 

At present, we are financing this work & resulting improvements from our own funds.

To sum up, funding is critical now for three reasons:
- to support the continuous discovery and needs of our early adopters,
- to progress beyond validated viability toward the full platform vision,
- to meet growing interest, which we can no longer sustain without additional support.

— How does this proposal meaningfully extend Scalus' reach beyond current early adopters, and why can't this phase proceed without further Treasury support now? — 

The current budget request is intended to support our ability to engage with new adopters (businesses and DApps/protocol builders), enhance existing functionalities, and continue building up the platform. The budget breakdown reflects this across three main areas:

- Ongoing maintenance (line item - MAN) and user support (ONB1, ONB2)
- Improvements and tunings (SC1, SC2, ADV1, MPL2, MPL5, TEST1)
- Development of new capabilities:
 - Advanced UPLC optimisations (ADV2–ADV4)
 - Acceleration of the development cycle (ONB3–ONB4, TEST2, INT1–INT4)

Thank you for those questions, if you need the further clarification, please let me know.
